original_question: For the trigonometric Abel differential equations x' = (a0 + a1 sin t + a2 cos t)x^3 + (b0 + b1 sin t + b2 cos t)x^2, is 3 the maximum possible number of 2pi-periodic limit cycles?
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, Problem 6: the specific six-parameter family of trigonometric Abel differential equations with linear sin t and cos t coefficients, and the question whether this family can have more than three 2π-periodic limit cycles. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact family, the exact differential equation, the 2π-periodicity, and the sharp numerical target 3 from the paper’s Problem 6. It is aimed at the right specific open problem, not the broader generalization stated immediately afterward as Problem 7. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
missing_details: State explicitly that the question ranges over all real parameters a0, a1, a2, b0, b1, b2 in R; the paper asks about the maximum over the whole family, not one fixed equation. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

Make explicit that x=x(t) is a real-valued 2π-periodic solution of a nonautonomous Abel equation; Section 2.4 first gives the general T-periodic Abel framework and then specializes here to T=2π. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

Define 'limit cycle' in the paper’s sense: a 2π-periodic solution that is isolated among all 2π-periodic solutions of the equation. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

Note the hidden but important convention that x(t)≡0 is always a 2π-periodic solution for this family and is counted among the limit cycles only when it is isolated. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
refined_question: For real parameters a0, a1, a2, b0, b1, b2 ∈ R, consider the 2π-periodic Abel differential equation dx/dt = (a0 + a1 sin t + a2 cos t)x^3 + (b0 + b1 sin t + b2 cos t)x^2, with x=x(t) real-valued. Is 3 the maximal number of 2π-periodic solutions that are isolated among all 2π-periodic solutions of this equation (that is, limit cycles), counting the solution x(t)≡0 whenever it is isolated? ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Section 2.4, Problem 6, because its displayed equation matches the paper’s displayed equation term-for-term. The nearby context on page 7 defines the general periodic Abel equation and the paper’s meaning of limit cycle, while the paragraph immediately after Problem 6 on page 8 adds the important scope note that x≡0 is always a periodic solution for this family. The same page then explicitly broadens the discussion to Problem 7, so the paper-faithful refinement should remain at the narrower Problem 6 level. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
